messages:
Maya: Hey folks, ACME reported a big jump in API latency for their production tenant starting ~09:10 UTC. p99 jumped from ~600ms to ~3s. They provided traces and a repro curl. Escalating to oncall.

Tom: thanks, Maya. Can you paste the repro curl and the dashboard link + screenshot? also any recent deploys? @Li FYI.

Maya: repro curl below and ticket INF-4321 with trace links. No deploys in that window per deploy-bot.

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <ACME_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-ggml-small","input":"hello world","stream":false}'
```

Maya: dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/tenant-latency (screenshots attached in ticket).

Li: looking at traces now. The trace samples from that tenant mostly show 400-800ms. The Prometheus panel for p99 shows ~3s. My hunch: rollup/sampling + histogram bucket aliasing.

Tom: can you share the PromQL used by the panel? maybe it's using a 5m rollup with stale buckets.

Li: panel runs this (copied from dashboard):

```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(api_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```

Li: but our rollup job pre-aggregates buckets every 10m for long retention, and the dashboard is pulling from the 10m rollup endpoint for that panel. So mismatched windows between the rollup and the panel's query could inflate upper quantiles.

Derek: +1. Also saw a config change yesterday: the ingest-side sampler for traces bumped from 0.1 -> 0.02 for that tenant group, which could bias which traces we look at (only the slow ones may be retained).

Tom: so two hypotheses: 1) rollup window mismatch causing p99 to be computed over coarse buckets, 2) trace sampling bias showing a different distribution. Which explains dashboard vs trace discrepancy. Any quick repro to prove it?

Maya: ACME says they can run a 10k request stress test on a staging key if we want to reproduce. They prefer a hotfix first.

Li: quick test: run the same curl loop with small QPS from my laptop against staging and compare raw histogram buckets vs rollup. I ran 500 reqs at 5 RPS earlier, and raw metrics p99=650ms, rollup p99=2.8s. Confirmed mismatch.

Li: root cause: our rollup job compresses buckets into fewer le boundaries for long retention (to save cardinality). When you run histogram_quantile over those coarse buckets, the interpolation lands higher.

Derek: mitigation options: 1) change dashboard to query raw recent series (no rollup) for 1h window, 2) tighten rollup to include fine buckets for recent 1h, 3) temporarily increase capacity / route tenant to dedicated pool, 4) flip ACME to fallback model with smaller latency.

Tom: recommended immediate actions: (A) update Grafana panel to use the /prometheus/raw endpoint or shorter range (1m-15m) so it doesn't hit long rollups, (B) ask infra to add fine-bucket retention for last 2h for tenant namespace, (C) ask support to run repro test on staging to validate.

Maya: I'll notify ACME that we're investigating and ask if they'd run the staging test. Also opened INF-4321 and linked this thread.

Li: I'll put a quick dashboard patch now (dash-change PR) to point to raw series and post the diff here.

sre-bot: deployed grafana patch to feature branch (ci/245). Panel now queries: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(api_request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le))` for the recent 30m range.

Derek: infra added a fine-bucket retention override for tenant: retention_override={tenant:acme, duration:2h, bucket_scheme:full}. Took ~30s to populate.

Tom: status update in 15m. If p99 still reads high, we'll consider routing to dedicated pool for ACME while we fix rollup logic.

Maya: ACME ran the staging test (5k requests, 10RPS). Traces and raw metrics show p99=720ms. Dashboard (patched) now shows ~740ms. Customer happy for now. They want a postmortem and permanent fix.

Li: will follow up with a short postmortem: root cause = rollup compression + panel querying long-rollup endpoint; contributing factor = reduced trace sampling making raw traces non-representative. Fixes: dashboard default to raw for last 1h, rollup change to keep full buckets for 2h, add alerting when dashboard/trace p99 delta > 25%.

Tom: thanks everyone. Maya, please close INF-4321 with notes + PR links: dash-change PR #712, infra-change PR #713. :thumbsup:

Maya: will do. Closing loop with ACME and adding next steps to the ticket. :white_check_mark:
